history.period: 1972-1992 (foundation stone laid 3 November 1972 by Nichidatsu Fujii; inaugurated 1 November 1992)
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - Buddhist Peace Pagoda (stupa) built by the Japanese Buddhist order Nipponzan-Myohoji; keep-or-drop decision needed. One of 80+ Peace Pagodas worldwide built under the guidance of Nichidatsu Fujii (1885-1985), founder of the Nipponzan-Myohoji order, who was inspired by Mahatma Gandhi's non-violence. Designed by M. Ohka and constructed in 36 months, the white pagoda stands 28.5 m tall and 23 m in diameter on the slopes of the Jalapahar hills. It houses four gold-polished statues of Buddha in different postures and eight sandstone carvings depicting stages of Buddha's life. The adjacent two-storey white Japanese Temple (Nipponzan Myohoji Buddhist Temple) has a prayer room where the chief priest beats a huge drum (Ho-ko); prayers are held 4:30-6:30 AM and 4:30-6:30 PM. The site is open to people of all faiths.

town_description: Darjeeling is a hill town in the Eastern Himalaya of West Bengal, famous for its tea, the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (a UNESCO World Heritage toy train) and views of Kanchenjunga. Founded as a British sanatorium and summer retreat in the 19th century, it blends colonial heritage with Tibetan Buddhist culture and is one of India's best-known tourist destinations.
